title: Model changelog: add immutable public_changelog_fields allowlist + redaction for internal-only metadata
author: Michael Nguyen
description: Context: As part of the model metadata schema v1 + customer-visible model changelog work, we need a hard guarantee that customer-facing release notes and feeds cannot accidentally include internal-only metadata fields (vendor details, internal nicknames, incident notes, etc.). This PR introduces an explicit allowlist called public_changelog_fields on each model_version record, enforces immutability after publication, and adds redaction logic at the registry boundary so downstream consumers (generator, control plane, docs publish) only ever see a sanitized view. Approach: (1) Add public_changelog_fields (set of field paths) to schema_v1 for model versions. (2) Add RegistryPublicView builder that returns a redacted ModelVersionPublic object; fields not in allowlist are either omitted or replaced with "[redacted]" depending on type. (3) Ensure change-event emission uses the public view for customer-facing payloads while retaining full internal payloads for audit/SIEM. (4) Enforce immutability: once a version has a published changelog entry (or once public_changelog_fields is set and locked), attempts to widen allowlist or mutate existing allowed fields are rejected unless performed via the explicit "supersede/correct" flow (handled by control plane; registry returns a stable error code). (5) Add unit tests for redaction + immutability + edge cases (nested objects, arrays, empty allowlist). Notes: This is intentionally conservative; we can expand allowlist defaults later once docs/style guide stabilizes. Checklist: - [x] Schema updated + migrations - [x] Validation rules added - [x] Redaction implemented for API read paths + event emission - [x] Tests - [x] Docs for internal operators (inline comments + README snippet)
commits: schema_v1: add public_changelog_fields to ModelVersion record
validation: enforce allowlist syntax (field paths) + immutability constraints
public view: add redaction helper + ModelVersionPublic builder
events: emit customer_safe_payload using public view; keep full payload for audit stream
tests: redaction coverage for nested objects, arrays, missing fields, and immutability rules
docs: add registry README section on public changelog surfaces + common gotchas
illustrative_snippet:
Example allowlist entries (field paths):
- identity.model_id
- identity.version_id
- identity.display_name
- capabilities.context_window_tokens
- capabilities.tool_calling.supported
- provenance.base_model
- provenance.finetune_dataset_summary
- performance.profile_id
- deprecation.sunset_date
Any field not present in public_changelog_fields will not be present in the public view used by the changelog generator.
review_conversation: Jordan Lee (review): The immutability logic looks good, but I want to be sure we can’t widen the allowlist post-publication. Right now it seems tied to `public_changelog_locked`. Where is that set, and can it be bypassed by direct writes?

Michael Nguyen (author): Good catch. In this PR I added server-side enforcement in the update handler: if a record has `public_changelog_locked=true` OR `published_changelog_entry_id != null`, we reject any change where the new allowlist is a strict superset of the old allowlist. Also, the storage layer only supports updates through the service API (no direct DB access in prod). I added a test for the superset case + a test that changing order doesn’t trigger false positives.

Quentin Harris (review): Can we clarify behavior for "omitted vs redacted"? For example, if `provenance.vendor` is not allowed, do we send `vendor: [redacted]` or drop the key entirely? Dropping keys is nicer for customers but might be confusing for template code.

Michael Nguyen (author): Agreed. For the customer_safe_payload we drop keys entirely (including nested keys) so templates don’t have to special-case `[redacted]`. The `[redacted]` string is only used for internal debug logs (guarded by env + not shipped to customer surfaces). I updated the code comments and tests to reflect that.

Marcus Lin (review): Please add an explicit denylist for obviously sensitive fields (vendor_contract_id, internal_nickname, incident_notes) so we have defense in depth in case someone mistakenly adds them to allowlist.

Michael Nguyen (author): Added `ALWAYS_INTERNAL_FIELDS` guard. Even if they’re present in public_changelog_fields we drop them and emit a validation error on write (400 with code MODEL_METADATA_PUBLIC_FIELD_DENIED). This also gives us an audit signal if someone tries it. Added tests.

Elliot Price (review): Can we add a short README section explaining how docs templates should reference allowed fields? Also, does this align with the style guide expectation that compatibility notes are always present?

Michael Nguyen (author): Added README section + updated default allowlist used by the generator fixtures to include capabilities + compatibility fields. This PR doesn’t enforce template requirements, but it ensures those fields are available when we choose to require them.
Jordan Lee (follow-up): One more: ensure customer_safe_payload never contains internal URLs (s3://, grafana links, internal confluence).

Michael Nguyen (author): Added URL scheme filtering for string fields in public view (drop values with s3://, gs://, https://grafana., https://confluence.). This is intentionally narrow to avoid false positives; we can expand later. Added a test case for internal eval_url removal.
release_notes: Internal: Adds public_changelog_fields allowlist and registry-level redaction to prevent internal-only model metadata from leaking into customer-visible changelog entries/feeds. Enforces immutability after publication; attempts to widen allowlist or publish denied fields are rejected with explicit error codes.
